sanskrit: evaṃvidhaṃ kārmukabhīmanādam; adīnavat satpuruṣottamābhyām dadarśa lokaḥ kurusṛñjayāś ca; tad dvairathaṃ bhīṣmadhanaṃjayābhyām
english: Such was that single combat between the two best of true men, fought without faintheartedness, terrible with the thunder of their bows: the whole world, and the Kurus and Sṛñjayas, beheld that duel of chariots waged by Bhīṣma and Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca drauṇir bhūriśravāḥ śalyaś citrasenaś ca māriṣa putraḥ sāṃyamaneś caiva saubhadraṃ samayodhayan
english: Saṃjaya said: Droṇa's son, Bhūriśravas, Śalya, and Citrasena, and the son of Saṃyamana too, O honored one, together gave battle to the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: saṃsaktam atitejobhis tam ekaṃ dadṛśur janāḥ pañcabhir manujavyāghrair gajaiḥ siṃhaśiśuṃ yathā
english: The people watched him, alone and locked in fight with those five tigers among men of surpassing valor, as one might watch a lion's cub set upon by elephants.

sanskrit: nābhilakṣyatayā kaś cin na śaurye na parākrame babhūva sadṛśaḥ kārṣṇer nāstre nāpi ca lāghave
english: In eluding aim, in heroism, in prowess, in mastery of weapons, and in nimbleness of hand, not one of them proved a match for the son of Kṛṣṇa's sister.

sanskrit: tathā tam ātmajaṃ yuddhe vikramantam ariṃdamam dṛṣṭvā pārtho raṇe yattaḥ siṃhanādam atho 'nadat
english: Beholding his son, that tamer of foes, displaying such prowess in the fight, Pārtha, intent in battle, then raised aloud a lion's roar.

sanskrit: pīḍayānaṃ ca tat sainyaṃ pautraṃ tava viśāṃ pate dṛṣṭvā tvadīyā rājendra samantāt paryavārayan
english: Seeing your grandson harrying that host, O lord of peoples, your warriors, O king of kings, surrounded him on every side.

sanskrit: dhvajinīṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ dīnaśatrur adīnavat pratyudyayau sa saubhadras tejasā ca balena ca
english: Undismayed, the bane of his enemies' spirit, the son of Subhadrā advanced to meet the bannered army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons, with fiery energy and with strength.

sanskrit: tasya lāghavamārgastham ādityasadṛśaprabham vyadṛśyata mahac cāpaṃ samare yudhyataḥ paraiḥ
english: As he fought his foes in battle, his great bow, kept ever in the path of swift movement and bright as the sun, was seen by all.

sanskrit: sa drauṇim iṣuṇaikena viddhvā śalyaṃ ca pañcabhiḥ dhvajaṃ sāṃyamaneś cāpi so 'ṣṭābhir apavarjayat
english: Piercing Droṇa's son with a single shaft and Śalya with five, with eight more he struck down the banner of Saṃyamana's son.

sanskrit: rukmadaṇḍāṃ mahāśaktiṃ preṣitāṃ saumadattinā śitenoragasaṃkāśāṃ patriṇā vijahāra tām
english: That mighty, gold-shafted spear, like a serpent, hurled at him by the son of Somadatta, he struck aside with a sharp winged arrow.

sanskrit: śalyasya ca mahāghorān asyataḥ śataśaḥ śarān nivāryārjunadāyādo jaghāna samare hayān
english: Warding off the hundreds of dreadful arrows that Śalya loosed, the heir of Arjuna slew his horses in the battle.

sanskrit: bhūriśravāś ca śalyaś ca drauṇiḥ sāṃyamaniḥ śalaḥ nābhyavartanta saṃrabdhāḥ kārṣṇer bāhubalāśrayāt
english: Bhūriśravas and Śalya, Droṇa's son, the son of Saṃyamana, and Śala—though furious, they could make no headway against the strength of the arm of Kṛṣṇa's nephew.

sanskrit: tatas trigartā rājendra madrāś ca saha kekayaiḥ pañcatriṃśatisāhasrās tava putreṇa coditāḥ
english: Then, O king of kings, the Trigartas and the Madras together with the Kekayas, five-and-thirty thousand strong, urged on by your son—

sanskrit: dhanurvedavido mukhyā ajeyāḥ śatrubhir yudhi sahaputraṃ jighāṃsantaṃ parivavruḥ kirīṭinam
english: foremost masters of the science of archery, unconquerable by foes in battle—closed in around the Diademed One, who, with his son, sought to destroy them.

sanskrit: tau tu tatra pitāputrau parikṣiptau ratharṣabhau dadarśa rājan pāñcālyaḥ senāpatir amitrajit
english: Those two bulls among charioteers, father and son, hemmed in there, the Pāñcāla commander, conqueror of foes, beheld, O king.

sanskrit: sa vāraṇarathaughānāṃ sahasrair bahubhir vṛtaḥ vājibhiḥ pattibhiś caiva vṛtaḥ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: Encircled by many thousands of floods of elephants and chariots, encircled too by horsemen and footmen by the hundred thousand,

sanskrit: dhanur visphārya saṃkruddhaś codayitvā varūthinīm yayau tan madrakānīkaṃ kekayāṃś ca paraṃtapaḥ
english: twanging his bow in wrath and urging on his host, that scorcher of foes advanced against that division of the Madrakas and the Kekayas.

sanskrit: tena kīrtimatā guptam anīkaṃ dṛḍhadhanvanā prayuktarathanāgāśvaṃ yotsyamānam aśobhata
english: Guarded by that glorious warrior of the steadfast bow, the division, with its chariots, elephants, and horses arrayed and eager for the fray, shone resplendent.

sanskrit: so 'rjunaṃ pramukhe yāntaṃ pāñcālyaḥ kurunandana tribhiḥ śāradvataṃ bāṇair jatrudeśe samarpayat
english: That Pāñcāla, O delight of the Kurus, struck the son of Śaradvat, who was advancing at the front toward Arjuna, with three arrows in the region of the collarbone.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa madrakān hatvā daśabhir daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ hṛṣṭa eko jaghānāśvaṃ bhallena kṛtavarmaṇaḥ
english: Then, slaying the Madrakas with shafts by tens upon tens, exulting and alone, he slew with a broad-headed arrow the horse of Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: damanaṃ cāpi dāyādaṃ pauravasya mahātmanaḥ jaghāna vipulāgreṇa nārācena paraṃtapaḥ
english: And Damana, heir of the great-souled Paurava, that scorcher of foes slew with a broad-pointed iron shaft.

sanskrit: tataḥ sāṃyamaneḥ putraḥ pāñcālyaṃ yuddhadurmadam avidhyat triṃśatā bāṇair daśabhiś cāsya sārathim
english: Then the son of Saṃyamana pierced the Pāñcāla, frenzied in battle, with thirty arrows, and his charioteer with ten.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho maheṣvāsaḥ sṛkkiṇī parisaṃlihan bhallena bhṛśatīkṣṇena nicakartāsya kārmukam
english: Deeply wounded, that mighty bowman, licking the corners of his mouth, cut his foe's bow asunder with an exceedingly sharp broad-headed arrow.

sanskrit: athainaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā kṣipram eva samarpayat aśvāṃś cāsyāvadhīd rājann ubhau tau pārṣṇisārathī
english: Then swiftly he struck him with five-and-twenty shafts, and slew his horses, O king, and both his flank-guarding charioteers.

sanskrit: sa hatāśve rathe tiṣṭhan dadarśa bharatarṣabha putraḥ sāṃyamaneḥ putraṃ pāñcālyasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Standing in his chariot whose horses were slain, O bull of the Bharatas, the son of Saṃyamana beheld the son of the great-souled Pāñcāla.

sanskrit: sa saṃgṛhya mahāghoraṃ nistriṃśavaram āyasam padātis tūrṇam abhyarchad rathasthaṃ drupadātmajam
english: Seizing a most dreadful and excellent iron scimitar, on foot he swiftly rushed upon the son of Drupada who stood in his chariot.

sanskrit: taṃ mahaugham ivāyāntaṃ khāt patantam ivoragam bhrāntāvaraṇanistriṃśaṃ kālotsṛṣṭam ivāntakam
english: As he came on like a great flood, like a serpent falling from the sky, whirling shield and scimitar, like Death loosed by Time itself,

sanskrit: dīpyantam iva śastrārcyā mattavāraṇavikramam apaśyan pāṇḍavās tatra dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ
english: blazing as it were with the flame of his weapon, with the stride of a maddened elephant—the Pāṇḍavas there beheld him, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: tasya pāñcālaputras tu pratīpam abhidhāvataḥ śitanistriṃśahastasya śarāvaraṇadhāriṇaḥ
english: But as he ran headlong to the encounter, sharp scimitar in hand and bearing his shield, the son of the Pāñcāla king—

sanskrit: bāṇavegam atītasya rathābhyāśam upeyuṣaḥ tvaran senāpatiḥ kruddho bibheda gadayā śiraḥ
english: as he passed beyond the rush of arrows and drew near to the chariot, the commander in his wrath made haste and split his head with his mace.

sanskrit: tasya rājan sanistriṃśaṃ suprabhaṃ ca śarāvaram hatasya patato hastād vegena nyapatad bhuvi
english: As he was slain and fell, O king, his scimitar and his bright shield dropped swiftly from his hand to the ground.

sanskrit: taṃ nihatya gadāgreṇa lebhe sa paramaṃ yaśaḥ putraḥ pāñcālarājasya mahātmā bhīmavikramaḥ
english: Having slain him with the head of his mace, the great-souled son of the Pāñcāla king, of terrible prowess, won the highest glory.

sanskrit: tasmin hate maheṣvāse rājaputre mahārathe hāhākāro mahān āsīt tava sainyasya māriṣa
english: When that mighty bowman, the prince and great car-warrior, was slain, a great cry of dismay arose from your army, O honored one.

sanskrit: tataḥ sāṃyamaniḥ kruddho dṛṣṭvā nihatam ātmajam abhidudrāva vegena pāñcālyaṃ yuddhadurmadam
english: Then the son of Saṃyamana, enraged at seeing his son slain, rushed with violence upon the Pāñcāla, that frenzied warrior.

sanskrit: tau tatra samare vīrau sametau rathināṃ varau dadṛśuḥ sarvarājānaḥ kuravaḥ pāṇḍavās tathā
english: Those two heroes, foremost of charioteers, met there in battle, and all the kings beheld them—the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas alike.

sanskrit: tataḥ sāṃyamaniḥ kruddhaḥ pārṣataṃ paravīrahā ājaghāna tribhir bāṇais tottrair iva mahādvipam
english: Then the wrathful son of Saṃyamana, slayer of enemy heroes, struck the son of Pṛṣata with three arrows, as one goads a great elephant with hooks.

sanskrit: tathaiva pārṣataṃ śūraṃ śalyaḥ samitiśobhanaḥ ājaghānorasi kruddhas tato yuddham avartata
english: Likewise Śalya, glorious in assemblies of battle, in his wrath struck the heroic son of Pṛṣata upon the breast; and thereupon the fight raged on.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca daivam eva paraṃ manye pauruṣād api saṃjaya yat sainyaṃ mama putrasya pāṇḍusainyena vadhyate
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Fate, I think, is higher than even human effort, Saṃjaya, in that my son's army is being slaughtered by the army of Pāṇḍu's sons.

sanskrit: nityaṃ hi māmakāṃs tāta hatān eva hi śaṃsasi avyagrāṃś ca prahṛṣṭāṃś ca nityaṃ śaṃsasi pāṇḍavān
english: For always, my dear, you report my own men as slain, while ever you tell of the Pāṇḍavas as untroubled and exultant.

sanskrit: hīnān puruṣakāreṇa māmakān adya saṃjaya patitān pātyamānāṃś ca hatān eva ca śaṃsasi
english: My own men, bereft of manly valor today, O Saṃjaya, you report as fallen, as being struck down, and as slain outright.

sanskrit: yudhyamānān yathāśakti ghaṭamānāñ jayaṃ prati pāṇḍavā vijayanty eva jīyante caiva māmakāḥ
english: Though they fight to the utmost of their power and strive for victory, still the Pāṇḍavas conquer, and my own are vanquished.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tīvrāṇi duḥkhāni duryodhanakṛtāni ca aśrauṣaṃ satataṃ tāta duḥsahāni bahūni ca
english: And so I have heard without ceasing, my dear, of the bitter sorrows wrought by Duryodhana, sorrows past bearing and beyond number.

sanskrit: tam upāyaṃ na paśyāmi jīyeran yena pāṇḍavāḥ māmakā vā jayaṃ yuddhe prāpnuyur yena saṃjaya
english: I can see no means whereby the Pāṇḍavas might be defeated, or whereby my own might win victory in the war, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca kṣayaṃ manuṣyadehānāṃ gajavājirathakṣayam śṛṇu rājan sthiro bhūtvā tavaivāpanayo mahān
english: Saṃjaya said: Hear, O king, with a steady heart, of the destruction of the bodies of men and the destruction of elephants, horses, and chariots—the great ruin that is the fruit of your own misrule.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tu śalyena pīḍito navabhiḥ śaraiḥ pīḍayām āsa saṃkruddho madrādhipatim āyasaiḥ
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna, harried by Śalya with nine arrows, in his fury harried the lord of the Madras in turn with iron shafts.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma pārṣatasya parākramam nyavārayata yat tūrṇaṃ śalyaṃ samitiśobhanam
english: There we beheld a marvel, the prowess of the son of Pṛṣata, in that he swiftly checked Śalya, the glory of the battle-line.

sanskrit: nāntaraṃ dadṛśe kaś cit tayoḥ saṃrabdhayo raṇe muhūrtam iva tad yuddhaṃ tayoḥ samam ivābhavat
english: No one could see any opening in those two, furious in the fray; for a while the combat between them seemed evenly matched.

sanskrit: tataḥ śalyo mahārāja dhṛṣṭadyumnasya saṃyuge dhanuś ciccheda bhallena pītena niśitena ca
english: Then Śalya, O great king, in the encounter cut asunder the bow of Dhṛṣṭadyumna with a sharp, yellow-feathered broad-headed arrow.

sanskrit: athainaṃ śaravarṣeṇa chādayām āsa bhārata giriṃ jalāgame yadvaj jaladā jaladhāriṇaḥ
english: And he covered him with a rain of arrows, O Bhārata, as the water-bearing clouds at the coming of the rains cover a mountain.

sanskrit: abhimanyus tu saṃkruddho dhṛṣṭadyumne nipīḍite abhidudrāva vegena madrarājarathaṃ prati
english: But Abhimanyu, enraged when Dhṛṣṭadyumna was thus hard pressed, rushed with violence against the chariot of the Madra king.

sanskrit: tato madrādhiparathaṃ kārṣṇiḥ prāpyātikopanaḥ ārtāyanim ameyātmā vivyādha viśikhais tribhiḥ
english: Then the son of Kṛṣṇa's sister, of immeasurable spirit, reaching in great wrath the chariot of the Madra lord, pierced the son of Ṛtāyana with three arrows.

sanskrit: tatas tu tāvakā rājan parīpsanto ''rjuniṃ raṇe madrarājarathaṃ tūrṇaṃ parivāryāvatasthire
english: Then your men, O king, eager to lay hold of Arjuna's son in the battle, swiftly surrounded the chariot of the Madra king and took their stand.

sanskrit: duryodhano vikarṇaś ca duḥśāsanaviviṃśatī durmarṣaṇo duḥsahaś ca citrasenaś ca durmukhaḥ
english: Duryodhana and Vikarṇa, Duḥśāsana and Viviṃśati, Durmarṣaṇa and Duḥsaha, Citrasena and Durmukha,

sanskrit: satyavrataś ca bhadraṃ te purumitraś ca bhārata ete madrādhiparathaṃ pālayantaḥ sthitā raṇe
english: and Satyavrata—bless you—and Purumitra, O Bhārata: these stood in the battle, guarding the chariot of the Madra lord.

sanskrit: tān bhīmasenaḥ saṃkruddho dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ draupadeyābhimanyuś ca mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau
english: Against them came Bhīmasena in his wrath, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata, the sons of Draupadī and Abhimanyu, and the two sons of Mādrī among the Pāṇḍavas,

sanskrit: nānārūpāṇi śastrāṇi visṛjanto viśāṃ pate abhyavartanta saṃhṛṣṭāḥ parasparavadhaiṣiṇaḥ te vai samīyuḥ saṃgrāme rājan durmantrite tava
english: loosing weapons of every kind, O lord of peoples, advancing in high exultation and seeking each other's death; and they met in combat, O king, because of your evil counsel.

sanskrit: tasmin dāśarathe yuddhe vartamāne bhayāvahe tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca prekṣakā rathino 'bhavan
english: While that terrible chariot-battle was being waged, the car-warriors of your side and of the enemy alike became mere onlookers.

sanskrit: śastrāṇy anekarūpāṇi visṛjanto mahārathāḥ anyonyam abhinardantaḥ saṃprahāraṃ pracakrire
english: Loosing weapons of many forms, those great car-warriors, roaring at one another, joined in the fierce encounter.

sanskrit: te yattā jātasaṃrambhāḥ sarve 'nyonyaṃ jighāṃsavaḥ mahāstrāṇi vimuñcantaḥ samāpetur amarṣaṇāḥ
english: Intent and seized with fury, all of them eager to slay one another, hurling great missiles and unable to brook the affront, they fell upon each other.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu saṃkruddho dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ mahāraṇe vivyādha niśitair bāṇaiś caturbhis tvarito bhṛśam
english: Duryodhana, enraged, in that great battle pierced Dhṛṣṭadyumna in haste and hard with four sharp arrows.

sanskrit: durmarṣaṇaś ca viṃśatyā citrasenaś ca pañcabhiḥ durmukho navabhir bāṇair duḥsahaś cāpi saptabhiḥ viviṃśatiḥ pañcabhiś ca tribhir duḥśāsanas tathā
english: And Durmarṣaṇa pierced him with twenty arrows and Citrasena with five, Durmukha with nine and Duḥsaha with seven, Viviṃśati with five, and Duḥśāsana with three.

sanskrit: tān pratyavidhyad rājendra pārṣataḥ śatrutāpanaḥ ekaikaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā darśayan pāṇilāghavam
english: In return the son of Pṛṣata, that tormentor of foes, O king of kings, struck them back, each one with five-and-twenty arrows, displaying the nimbleness of his hand.

sanskrit: satyavrataṃ tu samare purumitraṃ ca bhārata abhimanyur avidhyat tau daśabhir daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: And in the battle, O Bhārata, Abhimanyu pierced Satyavrata and Purumitra, those two, with ten arrows each.

sanskrit: mādrīputrau tu samare mātulaṃ mātṛnandanau chādayetāṃ śaravrātais tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: And the two sons of Mādrī, the delight of their mother, covered their maternal uncle in the battle with showers of arrows; and that was as it were a marvel.

sanskrit: tataḥ śalyo mahārāja svasrīyau rathināṃ varau śarair bahubhir ānarchat kṛtapratikṛtaiṣiṇau chādyamānau tatas tau tu mādrīputrau na celatuḥ
english: Then Śalya, O great king, assailed his two sister's sons, those foremost of charioteers, with many arrows, each side bent on repaying blow for blow; yet though so covered, the two sons of Mādrī did not waver.

sanskrit: atha duryodhanaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ vidhitsuḥ kalahasyāntaṃ gadāṃ jagrāha pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Then, catching sight of Duryodhana, the mighty Bhīmasena, that son of Pāṇḍu, wishing to make an end of the quarrel, took up his mace.

sanskrit: tam udyatagadaṃ dṛṣṭvā kailāsam iva śṛṅgiṇam bhīmasenaṃ mahābāhuṃ putrās te prādravan bhayāt
english: Seeing the mighty-armed Bhīmasena, mace raised on high like crested Kailāsa, your sons fled away in terror.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu saṃkruddho māgadhaṃ samacodayat anīkaṃ daśasāhasraṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ tarasvinām māgadhaṃ purataḥ kṛtvā bhīmasenaṃ samabhyayāt
english: But Duryodhana, enraged, urged on the king of Magadha, with his division of ten thousand swift elephants; and placing the Magadha king in the van, he advanced upon Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: āpatantaṃ ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā gajānīkaṃ vṛkodaraḥ gadāpāṇir avārohad rathāt siṃha ivonnadan
english: Seeing that host of elephants bearing down upon him, Vṛkodara, mace in hand, leapt down from his chariot, roaring aloud like a lion.

sanskrit: adrisāramayīṃ gurvīṃ pragṛhya mahatīṃ gadām abhyadhāvad gajānīkaṃ vyāditāsya ivāntakaḥ
english: Grasping his great, heavy mace, hard as the core of a mountain, he ran upon the elephant-host like Death with gaping jaws.

sanskrit: sa gajān gadayā nighnan vyacarat samare balī bhīmaseno mahābāhuḥ savajra iva vāsavaḥ
english: Smiting the elephants with his mace, the mighty, great-armed Bhīmasena ranged over the field like Vāsava wielding the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tasya nādena mahatā manohṛdayakampinā vyatyaceṣṭanta saṃhatya gajā bhīmasya nardataḥ
english: At the great roar of Bhīma as he bellowed, a roar that shook mind and heart, the elephants huddled together and writhed in confusion.

sanskrit: tatas tu draupadīputrāḥ saubhadraś ca mahārathaḥ nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ
english: Then the sons of Draupadī, and the son of Subhadrā, that great car-warrior, and Nakula and Sahadeva, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata,

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhaṃ bhīmasya rakṣantaḥ śaravarṣeṇa vāraṇān abhyadhāvanta varṣanto meghā iva girīn yathā
english: guarding Bhīma's rear, ran down upon the elephants with a rain of arrows, pouring it forth as clouds pour rain upon the mountains.

sanskrit: kṣuraiḥ kṣuraprair bhallaiś ca pītair añjalikair api pātayantottamāṅgāni pāṇḍavā gajayodhinām
english: With razor-edged shafts and razor-tipped arrows, with broad-heads and yellow-feathered shafts and crescent-headed darts, the Pāṇḍavas struck down the heads of the elephant-riders.

sanskrit: śirobhiḥ prapatadbhiś ca bāhubhiś ca vibhūṣitaiḥ aśmavṛṣṭir ivābhāti pāṇibhiś ca sahāṅkuśaiḥ
english: With heads falling down, and with ornamented arms, and with hands still grasping their goads, it seemed as though a hail of stones were raining down.

sanskrit: hṛtottamāṅgāḥ skandheṣu gajānāṃ gajayodhinaḥ adṛśyantācalāgreṣu drumā bhagnaśikhā iva
english: The elephant-riders, their heads struck off, were seen upon the shoulders of the elephants like trees with broken crests upon mountain peaks.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnahatān anyān apaśyāma mahāgajān patitān pātyamānāṃś ca pārṣatena mahātmanā
english: And we saw other great elephants slain by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, fallen and being struck down by the great-souled son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: māgadho 'tha mahīpālo gajam airāvatopamam preṣayām āsa samare saubhadrasya rathaṃ prati
english: Then the king of Magadha, lord of the earth, sent an elephant like Airāvata in the battle against the chariot of the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya māgadhasya gajottamam jaghānaikeṣuṇā vīraḥ saubhadraḥ paravīrahā
english: Beholding that splendid elephant of the Magadha king bearing down upon him, the heroic son of Subhadrā, slayer of enemy heroes, slew it with a single arrow.
